title: Optimizing Nursing Communication for Symptom Management in Hemodialysis: Development of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Web Predictive Model for Burden Classification and Evidence Navigation.
summary: The open-access primary article develops and evaluates an AI symptom-burden classifier for 1,866 hemodialysis patients, with feature selection, eight model families, held-out testing, calibration, decision-curve analysis and SHAP interpretation. Published in Journal of Nursing Management.
ai_technology: Elastic net/Boruta selection and eight classifiers, including XGBoost, predict mild versus severe symptom burden.
organization: Department of Public Service, The First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China

evidence.tested: The 1,866-patient cohort used a 70/30 train-test split, cross-validation, calibration, DCA and subgroup analyses.
evidence.unknown: External replication and real-world or clinical benefit were not established by the reviewed study
evidence.ai_role: Elastic net/Boruta selection and eight classifiers, including XGBoost, predict mild versus severe symptom burden.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
